## 0. Data integrity check

I first pulled raw OHLCV (387 rows, 2025-05-01 → 2026-11-12), then the indicator series, then the deterministic verified snapshot for 2026-11-12. **All indicator values from `get_indicators` match the verified snapshot exactly** (10-EMA 173.35, 50-SMA 185.08, 200-SMA 153.64, RSI 41.86, MACD −6.18 / signal −4.14 / hist −2.04, ATR 8.93). One caveat I will carry through the report: **the 12.33M volume on the 2026-11-12 row is the lightest in more than a month and may reflect an incomplete session** — I therefore do not draw volume conclusions from that single bar, only from the 11-05 → 11-11 sequence.

For transparency: 8 indicators were selected — `close_10_ema`, `close_50_sma`, `close_200_sma`, `macd`, `macds`, `rsi`, `atr`, `vwma` (rationale in §7). Bollinger band values are quoted **only** from the verified snapshot, not as a selected indicator.

## 1. Trend hierarchy: a long-term uptrend inside a medium-term breakdown

**Long-term (200-SMA): intact and still rising.**
- 200-SMA = **153.64**, up from 153.53 on 2026-11-09 (still ticking higher).
- Close 171.58 sits **+11.68% above** the 200-SMA.
- 50-SMA (185.08) > 200-SMA (153.64) by **31.4 points** — the golden-cross structure established earlier in 2026 remains firmly in place. A death cross is not remotely close on this data.

**Medium-term (50-SMA): broken.**
- 50-SMA = **185.08**, and it has **rolled over** — it peaked at 186.90 on 2026-10-30 and has declined every session since.
- Close is **−7.29% below** the 50-SMA. That is the single clearest statement in this report: the intermediate trend is down.

**Short-term (10-EMA): down, but decelerating.**
- 10-EMA = **173.35**; close is **−1.02% below** it. Price has been below the 10-EMA since 2026-11-02 (close 178.34 vs EMA 191.80).
- Critical nuance: the 10-EMA's daily rate of decline has collapsed. It fell **191.80 → 188.82 → 185.70 → 180.12 → 176.53** across 11-02 → 11-06 (roughly 3–5 points/session), but only **174.04 → 173.74 → 173.35** from 11-10 → 11-12 (~0.35–0.40/session). The short-term downtrend is **flattening into a basing attempt**, not accelerating.

**Price structure — lower highs, lower lows (factual, from tool OHLC):**
- Swing highs: **209.05 (10-09)** → 209.00 (10-12) → 201.72 (10-21) → 198.84 (10-26) → 175.40 (11-03) → 172.40 (11-11)
- Swing lows: **184.45 (10-16)** → 165.25 (11-03) → **152.60 (11-05)**
- Peak-to-trough: 209.00 (10-12 close) → 154.99 (11-05 close) = **−25.84%** in 17 trading sessions.
- Rebound since: 154.99 → 172.40 (11-11) = **+11.23%**; current 171.58 = **+10.70%** off that low.

The rebound is real but has **not** reclaimed a single moving average on a closing basis. That is a counter-trend bounce inside a broken medium-term structure, not a trend reversal — yet.

---

## 2. Momentum: washed out and stabilizing, but no buy trigger

**RSI = 41.86** (up from 42.40, and from the 11-10 reading of 39.18).
- The momentum collapse was extreme: RSI **76.29 (10-09) → 46.27 (10-16) → 25.42 (11-05)**. The 11-05 print is the **only sub-30 (oversold) reading in the entire 2026-07-15 → 2026-11-12 window**.
- It has since recovered to 41.86 — out of oversold, but still **below the 50 midline**. This is the "no-man's-land" zone: the washout is over, but momentum has not turned up. RSI is not yet a bullish signal; it is a *neutralized* one.

**MACD = −6.18, Signal = −4.14, Histogram = −2.04.**
- **Bearish signal-line crossover: 2026-10-16** (MACD 6.11 vs signal 6.93; it had been above on 10-15 at 7.66 vs 7.14). The histogram has been negative for **20 consecutive sessions**.
- **Bearish zero-line crossover: 2026-11-03** (MACD +0.55 on 11-02 → −0.85 on 11-03). Both MACD and signal are now below zero — the momentum regime is officially bearish.
- **But the histogram is contracting for four straight sessions:** −5.03 (11-06) → −4.28 → −3.59 → −2.71 → **−2.04 (11-12)**. The MACD *line* itself has ticked up from −6.54 (11-10) to −6.34 to −6.18.
- Honest interpretation: this is **deceleration of the decline driven mostly by the signal line catching down to price**, not a fresh bullish impulse. A histogram contraction inside negative territory routinely precedes both genuine bottoms *and* dead-cat pauses. It is a "stop chasing shorts here" signal, not a "buy" signal.

## 3. Volume / participation: the rebound is under-supplied

**VWMA = 175.94** — the close (171.58) is **−2.48% below** the volume-weighted average, meaning the volume-weighted center of recent trade sits *above* the current price. Buyers are, on average, underwater. That is distribution, not accumulation.

More telling is the VWMA's relationship to the simple 20-day basis (183.26): VWMA is **7.3 points below** it, which implies **heavier volume transacted at lower prices** than the time-weighted average — i.e., selling pressure has carried the volume.

The bounce has attracted **no institutional participation**. Until volume expands on an up-close, rallies toward 176–185 should be treated as supply to sell into.

## 4. Volatility and risk: register has expanded, size down

- **ATR = 8.93**, equal to **5.21% of the 171.58 close**. The ATR has come down from a local peak of **9.72 on 2026-11-09** but remains far above the ~6.0–6.3 readings of early October (6.00 on 10-07, 6.27 on 10-02). Volatility roughly **+45%** versus that baseline.
- **Bollinger bands (verified snapshot): middle 183.26, upper 212.08, lower 154.44.** Band width = 57.64 points = **31.4% of the middle band** — an exceptionally wide envelope, confirming a volatility-expansion regime.
- **%B = (171.58 − 154.44) / 57.64 = 0.30** — price sits in the **lower third** of the bands. It is *not* pinned to the lower band (the 11-05 low of 152.60 printed essentially on it), which is consistent with a bounce rather than a fresh breakdown in the very short term.

Practical implication: **stops must be at least 1.5–2.0 ATR (13–18 points) wide** to survive routine noise, and position size must be cut accordingly.

## 6. Forward scenarios and actionable plans

*(Scenario probabilities below are my judgment, not tool output.)*

**Scenario A — Bear continuation / retest of the 200-SMA (≈45%).**
Trigger: a close below **168.25**, confirmation below **165.25**, on volume expanding back above ~30M.
Path: 165.25 → 154.99/152.60 → lower Bollinger 154.44 / 200-SMA 153.64.
Trade: short/underweight; entry on a failed rally into **173–176** (10-EMA/VWMA) rather than chasing at 171; **stop above 185.08** (the 50-SMA) or tighter at **>178.5** (1 ATR above the VWMA) for aggressive accounts; first target 155, second 154.4/153.6, extension 146–143.

**Scenario B — Base-building rebound (≈35%).**
Trigger: a **close above 175.94 (VWMA)** accompanied by volume > 30M, then a hold of the 10-EMA as support on any back-test.
Path: 183.26 (Boll middle) → 185.08 (50-SMA). A decisive close above 185.08 neutralizes the medium-term damage and reopens 196–199.
Trade: for longs, **wait for the volume-confirmed reclaim** — buying at 171.58 with the VWMA above price and the 50-SMA falling is buying into overhead supply. First add on a close > 176, second on a close > 185, stop 1.5 ATR (~13 points) beneath the trigger.

**Scenario C — Capitulation flush through the confluence (≈20%).**
Trigger: a close below **153.64** on volume > 50M (the 11-03/11-05 magnitude).
Path: 143.28 (08-04 low) → the 126.96–143.28 gap. This would be the first close below the 200-SMA in this dataset's recent history and would flip the long-term structure.
Trade: this is a regime change, not a dip. Reduce exposure mechanically on the close below 153.64; do not attempt to catch the gap fill.

**Position-sizing math (using ATR, not round numbers):** with ATR at 8.93, a 2-ATR stop is **17.86 points (10.4%)**. On a $1,000,000 book risking 1.00% ($10,000) per position: 10,000 / 17.86 ≈ **560 shares ≈ $96,000 notional (9.6% of book)**. Because ATR is ~45% above its early-October baseline, **notional exposure per unit of risk should be roughly one-third smaller than it was three weeks ago.**

**Hard rules I would apply right now:** (1) do not short into the 200-SMA confluence — the risk/reward is inverted there; (2) do not buy simply because RSI left oversold; require a *close* above the VWMA with volume; (3) treat 185.08 as the objective arbiter — above it the dip is a correction in an uptrend, below it the trend has changed.

---

## 7. Why these 8 indicators

| `close_200_sma` | The 153.64 level coincides with the 11-05 low and the lower Bollinger band — the single most consequential confluence in the chart. Essential for defining the line between "correction" and "regime change." |

| `rsi` | The 25.42 reading on 11-05 marks the momentum washout; 41.86 quantifies that it is no longer oversold without being bullish. Divergence monitoring for the next leg. |
| `atr` | Non-negotiable in a 5.2%-of-price volatility regime. Drives stop width (1.5–2 ATR) and position sizing; also used to normalize every level distance above. |
| `vwma` | The decisive tiebreaker for the bounce: price below VWMA (175.94) plus a VWMA below the 20-day simple basis proves the rebound is under-supplied. Price-only indicators cannot show this. |

*Deliberately excluded:* Bollinger upper/lower as selected indicators (redundant with 200-SMA/ATR in this setup — the band values are still cited from the verified snapshot because of the confluence), `boll` middle (collinear with 50-SMA in the 183–185 zone), and MACD histogram as a separate call (derivable from `macd` − `macds`).

## PLTR Sentiment Report — 2026-11-05 to 2026-11-12

**Data-quality preamble (read first):** Only one of the three configured sources produced data. Yahoo Finance news returned a hard `DATA_UNAVAILABLE` (YFDataException), and all three Reddit communities returned fetch failures. Per the source notes, these are absences of data, **not** evidence of silence about PLTR. Consequently this report rests entirely on 19 on-topic StockTwits messages, and the institutional/news half of the usual cross-source check is simply missing. Confidence is therefore **low**, and the band should be treated as a weak, single-source lean rather than a settled read.

---

### 1. Source-by-source breakdown

**News (Yahoo Finance, past 7 days) — UNAVAILABLE.**
No headlines were retrievable; no institutional framing, event calendar, or analyst commentary could be assessed. I have not substituted or estimated anything. This is the single biggest limitation of this report: the slower-moving, fact-based signal that normally anchors the read (earnings dates, contract awards, index/flow news, regulatory items) is entirely absent, so any "catalyst" below is retail chatter rather than confirmed event.

**StockTwits — 19 on-topic posts of 30 fetched.**
- Classifier read of all on-topic posts (screened by Jev): **5 bullish / 6 bearish / 4 neutral / 4 unclear** — a slightly net-negative tilt.
- User self-tags: **3 Bullish (16%) / 3 Bearish (16%) / 13 unlabeled** — i.e. the visible bull/bear tag ratio is 1:1, and ~68% of posters declined to label a stance.
- The gap between the two readings matters: the classifier finds more bearish than bullish content because several *unlabeled* posts carry clearly defensive or mocking framing. This is not an enthusiastic crowd; it is a crowd that is talking mostly without conviction tags.
- **Bearish-leaning content, with specifics:** @thefloofer posts repeatedly with price-anchored pessimism — "169.11 never forget", "this 180 looks funny", "getting set up for some nice dips", "prolly open at around 120" (five separate posts; no label, but functionally a de-rating narrative). @openclassaction2 offers the most substantive bear case in the dataset: "index and retirement money own the multiple now, not just the believers… when a story stock lives in pension portfolios, a normal drawdown stops being normal," and "contracts renew on budgets, multiples renew on belief… when belief gets repriced, even signed work trades like a hope trade." @ST_Tropez_Trading is explicitly Bearish twice, including mockery ("Small hat uber stock will weather any storm 😂"). @onceuponatime23 (Bearish) is political: "so now that the dems won, karp says middle east war and domestic surveillance are 'progressive' lmao. they don't even hide the grift."
- **Bullish content:** @BIGbash08oo — "major European deals INBOUND" and "Bullish AF" (a forward-looking catalyst claim, unverified); @Series4Guy tagged Bullish with a link; @AshHydrogen — "$SPY $NVDA has the circular financing… $PLTR just makes BILLIONS EVERY QUARTER" (fundamentals-over-narrative argument); @albabynyr — an exit at ~$175 with a defensive explanation of why he sold and did not short.
- **Noise:** @SilverEagle's Thiel/"Antichrist" post and @kind22's "sorry no funding" add no directional information.

**Reddit (r/wallstreetbets, r/stocks, r/investing) — UNAVAILABLE.**
All three fetches failed. No community read, no long-form bull/bear essays, and no r/investing long-horizon counterweight. Explicitly **not** an absence of discussion.

---

### 2. Cross-source divergences and alignments

With two of three sources dark, the standard institutional-vs-retail divergence test **cannot be run** for PLTR this week, and I flag that as a real gap rather than inferring a mismatch.

What *is* observable is an **intra-StockTwits divergence**, and it is the most informative thing in this dataset:
- **Business/fundamental bulls** ("major European deals INBOUND", "makes BILLIONS EVERY QUARTER", "amazing volume") are pointing at revenue and contract momentum.
- **Price-action and multiple bears** are pointing at the stock's *valuation regime*, not the business ("belief gets repriced", "even signed work trades like a hope trade", "getting set up for some nice dips").
That split — company fine, multiple broken — is the classic shape of a post-de-rating tape. Posts referencing $169.11, $175, and $180 as past levels, alongside a "prolly open at around 120" remark, imply a very large drawdown in the visible conversation. **These price levels are unverified user claims, not tool-sourced data**, and I am citing them as evidence of tone, not as confirmed quotes.

Alignment: both explicitly-tagged bulls and the loudest unlabeled posters agree the **volume/liquidity environment is abnormal** ("amazing volume", "index and retirement money own the multiple now"), just with opposite interpretations — bulls read participation, bears read fragility.

---

### 3. Dominant narrative themes

1. **Post-drawdown disbelief and bag-holder humor** — the single most recurring tone ("169.11 never forget", "this 180 looks funny", "getting set up for some nice dips", exit disclosures at ~$175). Retail is anchored to old highs and expects further weakness rather than a V-recovery.
2. **Belief-vs-budget / multiple-repricing thesis** — the most intellectually substantive thread (@openclassaction2 ×2). The argument: PLTR's multiple is now underwritten by passive/index/pension ownership, and multiple compression can hurt even with signed contracts intact. This is a structural bear case, not a momentum complaint.
3. **Political and reputational exposure** — Karp's post-election framing ("the dems won… middle east war and domestic surveillance as 'progressive'"), "grift" accusations, and Thiel name-drops. Political/headline risk is showing up as a live sentiment lever in a way that is unusual relative to typical PLTR chatter.
4. **International contract momentum** — "major European deals INBOUND" is the only forward catalyst claim in the dataset, and it is unsourced.
5. **Liquidity/ownership structure** — volume and passive ownership discussed as a top-two topic, which normally signals a stock whose movement is flow-driven rather than news-driven right now.

---

### 4. Catalysts and risks surfaced by the data

**Catalysts (all unverified chatter — no news feed available to confirm or date them):**
- European contract announcements ("major European deals INBOUND", @BIGbash08oo), which if real would be the cleanest positive event risk.
- Continued quarterly revenue strength ("BILLIONS EVERY QUARTER", @AshHydrogen) as a fundamental counter to multiple-compression arguments.
- Elevated volume ("amazing volume") — could mark capitulation/exhaustion, but direction is undetermined.

**Risks:**
- **Multiple de-rating under passive ownership** — the dominant bear thesis; implies drawdowns can overshoot because index/pension holders are price-insensitive until they aren't.
- **Political/regulatory headline risk** post-election, with Karp's public positioning drawing "grift" framing from retail — reputationally loaded and hard to model.
- **Thin dip-buying support** — retail tone is cynical and expectant of "nice dips", not eager to add; that removes a stabilizer.
- **Information vacuum** — with news and Reddit dark, any real catalyst this week would not appear in this dataset at all; treat the read as blind to events.
- **Small sample** — 19 messages, only 3 explicit bull tags and 3 explicit bear tags. A handful of posters (@thefloofer, @ST_Tropez_Trading) account for a large share of the visible bearish content, so the tilt is partially a personality effect rather than a crowd effect.

---

### 5. Key sentiment signals

| Direction | Source | Supporting evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Bearish (weak) | StockTwits classifier | 5 bullish vs 6 bearish of 19 on-topic posts; 4 neutral, 4 unclear — net-negative with a large non-committal bloc |
| Neutral / undecided | StockTwits user tags | 3 Bullish (16%) / 3 Bearish (16%) / 13 unlabeled (68%) — explicit tags at 1:1, no conviction |
| Bearish | StockTwits @thefloofer (×5, unlabeled) | "169.11 never forget", "this 180 looks funny", "getting set up for some nice dips", "prolly open at around 120" — anchors to prior highs, expects lower |
| Bearish (structural) | StockTwits @openclassaction2 (×2, unlabeled) | "index and retirement money own the multiple now"; "when belief gets repriced, even signed work trades like a hope trade" |
| Bearish (political) | StockTwits @onceuponatime23 (tagged Bearish) | Karp post-election commentary dismissed as "grift" |
| Bearish (mocking) | StockTwits @ST_Tropez_Trading (×2, tagged Bearish) | "Small hat uber stock will weather any storm 😂"; one blank bearish tag |
| Bullish (fundamental) | StockTwits @AshHydrogen (unlabeled) | "$PLTR just makes BILLIONS EVERY QUARTER" contrasted with $NVDA "circular financing" |
| Bullish (catalyst claim) | StockTwits @BIGbash08oo (×2, tagged Bullish) | "major European deals INBOUND"; "Bullish AF" — unverified |
| Bullish (flow/volume) | StockTwits @thefloofer, @BIGbash08oo | "amazing volume" — read as participation by bulls, fragility by bears |
| Sold / de-risked | StockTwits @albabynyr | Sold balance of position "around $175", explains he did not short — prior holder now flat, unverified level |
| No signal | Yahoo Finance news | `DATA_UNAVAILABLE` (YFDataException) — institutional framing entirely missing |
| No signal | Reddit (WSB / stocks / investing) | All three fetches failed — not evidence of absent discussion |

---

**Bottom line:** A single live source shows PLTR retail sentiment bruised but not panicked: explicit bull/bear tags are dead even, the underlying post-level read is modestly negative, and the dominant tone is anchored-to-old-highs cynicism combined with a genuine debate about whether the multiple (not the business) is breaking. That is a **Mildly Bearish (score 4.1)** read at **low confidence**, driven by two dark sources and a 19-message sample. This is sentiment signal for the trader to weigh against fundamentals and technicals — not a price call — and any PLTR-specific event this week would sit outside this dataset entirely.
